DelegatedAuthorityGrant.description:
Scoped authority delegated to this principal for another principal's work.

Delegated authority is part of the native AIP identity model. It lets a
runtime distinguish "can read or operate on my own work" from "can read or
operate on work owned by a specific principal" without granting broad
`*:any` scopes. Compatibility profiles may project this from their own
auth systems, but the resulting grant is evaluated by AIP core/runtime
semantics.

scopes.description: Granted scope labels. `*` grants all scopes for this principal.

expires_at.description: Expiration timestamp. Expired grants MUST be ignored by runtimes.

approval request's `input_snapshot` evidence artifact.

TransactionRequest.description:
First-class request to execute a transactional AIP action.

`Action.transaction` remains the canonical semantic context for the
operation. This wrapper makes transaction workflows explicit on the wire so
gateways and runtimes can route, audit, and validate plan/commit/compensate
flows without embedding transaction commands inside adapter-specific JSON.

transaction_id.description: Stable transaction id for correlation across plan, commit, and compensation.

reason.description: Human-readable reason for policy, approval, and audit systems.

metadata.description: Optional request metadata for scheduling, audit, or transport bindings.

provider_operation.description: Durable provider operation reference for reconciliation.

reconciliation_cursor.description: Opaque cursor from the preceding reconciliation attempt.

ProviderOperationRef.description: Durable reference to an operation accepted by an external provider.

request_id.description: Optional provider request or trace id.

TransactionResult.description: Result of a first-class transactional AIP action.

transaction_id.description: Stable transaction id from the request or action context.

result.description: Final action result when execution reached a handler.

error.description: Protocol-level failure when no valid action result exists.

receipt_chain.description: Receipt chain proving the transaction decision or terminal state.

provider_operation.description: Durable provider operation reference used for reconciliation.

reconciliation_cursor.description: Opaque provider cursor used to continue reconciliation.

reconcile_after.description: Earliest time at which reconciliation should be retried.

The provider may have committed, but no definitive result is available.
Provider state is being reconciled before retry or compensation.
Reconciliation established the durable provider outcome.

TransactionPlan.description:
Durable execution plan produced by a transactional `Plan` action.

The plan is protocol-visible evidence for a later `Commit`. It captures the
exact action input hash, capability binding, relevant enterprise policy
metadata, and identity snapshot so runtimes can reject commits that no
longer match the planned operation.

transaction_id.description: Stable transaction id for the plan.

capability_id.description: Capability the plan was produced for.

compensation.description: Compensation contract available for the planned operation.

This policy never carries raw credential material. It only describes the

verify before dispatching an action to a connector or downstream system.

ResourceAccessPolicy.description:
Native resource read policy used by discovery and operational read APIs.

The policy is intentionally generic: product-specific ACL objects remain in
adapters, while AIP resources publish the minimal principal/scope/tenant
requirements needed by gateways and runtimes to avoid leaking resource
metadata across trust boundaries.
